answer: Make extra names expensive by pricing them on a cluster curve. To earn, an account freezes a deposit for two settlements, and the amount rises with how many other names share its funding graph, clock skew, or host measurements. Unlocking requires three established sureties, chosen from distant regions of a public atlas of runtime fingerprints, to countersign one unique work trace. One honest operator can keep a single orchard of work at modest cost. A cloned tundra of empty names faces a steepening bill, and a fingerprint collision slashes the whole cluster.
